source_text: Περὶ μὲν οὖν σωφροσύνης τοσοῦτον εἶπεν· ,,Ὅς ἂν ἐμβλέψῃ γυναικὶ πρὸς τὸ ἐπιθυμῆσαι αὐτῆς, ἤδη ἐμοίχευσε τῇ καρδίᾳ παρὰ τῷ θεῷ“. Καί· ,,Εἰ ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου ὁ δεξιὸς σκανδαλίζει σε, ἔκκοψον αὐτόν· συμφέρει γάρ σοι μονόφθαλμον εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν, ἢ μετὰ τῶν δύο πεμφθῆναι εἰς τὸ αἰώνιον πῦρ“. Καί· ,,Ὃς γαμεῖ ἀπολελυμένην ἀφ᾿ ἑτέρου ἀνδρός, μοιχᾶται“. Καί· ,,Εἰσί τινες οἵτινες εὐνουχίσθησαν ὑπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων, εἰσὶ δὲ οἵ ἐγεννήθησαν εὐνοῦχοι, εἰσὶ δὲ οἵ εὐνούχισαν ἑαυτοὺς διὰ τὴν βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν· πλήν οὐ πάντες τοῦτο χωροῦσιν“. Ὥσπερ καὶ οἱ νόμῳ ἀνθρωπίνῳ διγαμίας ποιούμενοι ἁμαρτωλοὶ παρὰ τῷ· ἡμετέρῳ διδασκάλῳ εἰσί, καὶ οἱ προσβλέποντες γυναικὶ πρὸς τὸ ἐπιθυμῆσαι αὐτῆς· οὐ γὰρ μόνον ὁ μοιχεύων ἔργῳ ἐκβέβληται παρ᾿ αὐτῷ, ἀλλὰ καὶ ὁ μοιχεῦσαι βουλόμενος, ὡς οὐ τῶν ἔργων φανερῶν μόνον τῷ θεῷ ἀλλὰ καὶ τῶν ἐνθυμημάτων. Καὶ πολλοί τινες καὶ πολλαὶ ἑξηκοντοῦται καὶ ἑβδομηκοντοῦται, οἵ ἐκ παίδων ἐμαθητεύθησαν τῷ Χριστῷ, ἄφθοροι διαμένουσι· καὶ εὔχομαι κατὰ πᾶν γένος ἀνθρώπων τοιούτους δεῖξαι. Τί γὰρ καὶ λέγομεν τὸ ἀναρίθμητον πλῆθος τῶν ἐξ ἀκολασίας μεταβαλόντων καὶ ταῦτα μαθόντων; οὐ γὰρ τοὺς δικαίους οὐδὲ τοὺς σώφρονας εἰς μετάνοιαν ἐκάλεσεν ὁ Χριστός, ἀλλὰ τοὺς ἀσεβεῖς καὶ ἀκολάστους καὶ ἀδίκους. Εἶπε δὲ οὕτως· ,,Οὐκ ἦλθον καλέσαι δικαίους, ἀλλὰ ἁμαρτωλοὺς εἰς μετάνοιαν“. Θέλει γὰρ ὁ πατὴρ ὁ οὐράνιος τὴν μετάνοιαν τοῦ ἁμαρτωλοῦ ἢ τὴν κόλασιν αὐτοῦ. Περὶ δὲ τοῦ στέργειν ἅπαντας ταῦτα ἐδίδαξεν· ,,Εἰ ἀγαπᾶτε τοὺς ἀγαπῶντας ὑμᾶς, τί καινὸν ποιεῖτε; καὶ γὰρ οἱ πόρνοι τοῦτο ποιοῦσιν. Ἐγὼ δὲ ὑμῖν λέγω· Εὔχεσθε ὑπὲρ τῶν ἐχθρῶν ὑμῶν καὶ ἀγαπᾶτε τοὺς μισοῦντας ὑμᾶς καὶ εὐλογεῖτε τοὺς καταρωμένους ὑμῖν καὶ εὔχεσθε ὑπὲρ τῶν ἐπηρεαζόντων ὑμᾶς“. Εἰς δὲ τὸ κοινωνεῖν τοῖς δεομένοις καὶ μηδὲν πρὸς δόξαν ποιεῖν ταῦτα ἔφη· ,,Παντὶ τῷ αἰτοῦντι δίδοτε καὶ τὸν βουλόμενον δανείσασθαι μὴ ἀποστραφῆτε. Εἰ γὰρ δανείζετε παρ᾿ ὧν ἐλπίζετε λαβεῖν, τί καινὸν ποιεῖτε; τοῦτο καὶ οἱ τελῶναι ποιοῦσιν. Ὑμεῖς δὲ μὴ θησαυρίζητε ἑαυτοῖς ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, ὅπου σὴς καὶ βρῶσις ἀφανίζει καὶ λῃσταὶ διορύσσουσι· θησαυρίζετε δὲ ἑαυτοῖς ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς, ὅπου οὔτε σὴς οὔτε βρῶσις ἀφανίζει. Τί γὰρ ὠφελεῖται ἄνθρωπος, ἂν τὸν κόσμον ὅλον κερδήσῃ, τὴν δὲ ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ἀπολέσῃ; ἢ τί δώσει αὐτῆς ἀντάλλαγμα; θησαυρίζετε οὖν ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς, ὅπου οὔτε σὴς οὔτε βρῶσις ἀφανίζει“. Καί· ,,Γίνεσθε δὲ χρηστοὶ καὶ οἰκτίρμονες, ὡς καὶ ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν χρηστός ἐστι καὶ οἰκτίρμων, καὶ τὸν ἥλιον αὐτοῦ ἀνατέλλει ἐπὶ ἁμαρτωλοὺς καὶ δικαίους καὶ πονηρούς. Μὴ μεριμνᾶτε δὲ τί φάγητε ἢ τί ἐνδύσησθε. Οὐχ ὑμεῖς τῶν πετεινῶν καὶ τῶν θηρίων διαφέρετε; καὶ ὁ θεὸς τρέφει αὐτά. Μὴ οὖν μεριμνήσητε τί φάγητε ἢ τί ἐνδύσησθε· οἶδε γὰρ ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ οὐράνιος ὅτι τούτων χρείαν ἔχετε. Ζητεῖτε δὲ τὴν βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν, καὶ ταῦτα πάντα προστεθήσεται ὑμῖν. Ὅπου γὰρ ὁ θησαυρός ἐστιν, ἐκεῖ καὶ ὁ νοῦς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου“. Καί· ,,Μὴ ποιῆτε ταῦτα πρὸς τὸ θεαθῆναι ὑπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων· εἰ δὲ μή γε, μισθὸν οὐκ ἔχετε παρὰ τοῦ πατρὸς ὑμῶν τοῦ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς“.
pass_a_gloss: He spoke thus about chastity: 'Whoever looks at a woman to desire her has already committed adultery with her in his heart.' And: 'If your right eye causes you to stumble, cut it out; it is better for you to enter the kingdom of heaven with one eye than to be thrown into eternal fire with two eyes.' And: 'Whoever marries a woman divorced from another man commits adultery.' And: 'There are some who have been castrated by men, there are some who were born eunuchs, and there are some who have castrated themselves for the kingdom of heaven; but not all can accept this.' Just as those who remarry according to human law are sinners in the eyes of our teacher, so also are those who look at a woman to desire her; for not only is the one who commits adultery in deed cast out by Him, but also the one who desires to commit adultery, as God is not only aware of visible deeds but also of thoughts. And many men and women, who from childhood were disciples of Christ, remain pure; and I pray that such people may be shown in every kind of human being. For what can we say about the countless number of people who have learned these things? For Christ did not call the righteous or the chaste to repentance, but the unrighteous and the unchaste. He said: 'I did not come to call the righteous, but the unrighteous to repentance.' The heavenly Father wants the repentance of the unrighteous rather than their punishment. But about loving all people, He taught: 'If you love those who love you, what are you doing that is new? Even the prostitutes do this. But I tell you: Pray for your enemies and love those who hate you and bless those who curse you and pray for those who mistreat you.' And about sharing with those in need and not doing these things for show, He said: 'Give to everyone who asks you, and do not turn away from anyone who wants to borrow from you. If you lend to those from whom you expect to receive, what are you doing that is new? Even the tax collectors do this. But do not store up treasures for yourselves on earth, where moth and rust destroy and thieves break in; store up treasures for yourselves in heaven, where neither moth nor rust destroys. For what does it profit a person to gain the whole world but lose his soul? Or what can he give in exchange for his soul? So store up treasures for yourselves in heaven, where neither moth nor rust destroys.' And: 'Be merciful and compassionate, just as your Father is merciful and compassionate, and He causes His sun to rise on the unrighteous and the righteous and the evil. Do not worry about what you will eat or what you will wear. Are you not different from the birds and the beasts? And God feeds them. So do not worry about what you will eat or what you will wear; for your heavenly Father knows that you need these things. Seek the kingdom of heaven, and all these things will be added to you. For where your treasure is, there your heart will be.' And: 'Do not do these things to be seen by people; if you do, you will have no reward from your Father in heaven.'

pass_b_english: Concerning self-control, Jesus spoke with uncompromising clarity: anyone who looks at a woman with lustful intent has already committed adultery with her in his heart before God (Matt 5:27–28). He pressed the point further: if your right eye causes you to stumble, gouge it out and throw it away; it is far better to enter the kingdom of heaven with one eye than to keep both and be cast into eternal fire (Matt 5:29–30). He also declared that whoever marries a woman divorced from another man commits adultery (Matt 5:31–32). Then he acknowledged the reality of celibacy: some are made eunuchs by others, some are born so, and some renounce marriage for the sake of the kingdom of heaven — though not everyone can accept this calling (Matt 5:33–34).

Just as those who remarry under human law are regarded as sinners by our Teacher, so too are those who look at a woman to desire her; for God does not merely judge outward acts — he also sees the heart. Not only is the one who commits adultery in deed cast out, but also the one who desires to commit adultery, since nothing is hidden from God, not even our thoughts (Matt 5:27–28). Many men and women, disciples from childhood, have remained pure into their sixties and seventies; I pray that such chastity may appear in every kind of human being. What then shall we say of the countless multitude who turned from licentiousness when they heard these words? Christ did not call the righteous or the self-controlled to repentance, but the ungodly, the unchaste, and the unjust. He said plainly, 'I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance' (Matt 5:38–42). The heavenly Father desires the sinner's repentance, not his punishment.

On the duty of loving all people, he taught: 'If you love only those who love you, what credit is that to you? Even prostitutes do as much. But I say to you: pray for your enemies, love those who hate you, bless those who curse you, pray for those who mistreat you' (Matt 5:43–48). On generosity and the rejection of display, he said: 'Give to everyone who asks, and do not turn away the one who wants to borrow. If you lend only to those you expect to repay, what is remarkable in that? Even tax collectors do the same. Do not store up treasures on earth, where moth and rust consume and thieves break in and steal; store up treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust destroys. What does it profit a person to gain the whole world yet forfeit his soul? Or what can anyone give in exchange for his soul? So lay up treasure in heaven, where neither moth nor rust destroys' (Matt 6:19–21).

'Be merciful and compassionate, just as your Father is merciful and compassionate; he makes his sun rise on the evil and the good, on the just and the unjust. Do not worry about what you will eat or what you will wear. Are you not worth far more than the birds and the wild animals? God feeds them. So do not be anxious about food or clothing; your heavenly Father knows you need these things. Seek first the kingdom of heaven, and all these things will be added to you. For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also' (Matt 6:25–34). 'Take care not to practice your righteousness before others to be seen by them; if you do, you will have no reward from your Father in heaven' (Matt 6:19–21).

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Greek text, including the specific numbers 'sixties and seventies' (ἑξηκοντοῦται καὶ ἑβδομηκοντοῦται) which Pass A omitted but Pass B correctly included. Scripture citations in Pass B are correctly mapped to the content and follow the required format. Pass A and B are consistent with the Greek source.
